summary: Fred Barthelet, CTO and co-founder of Alpic, presents a deep dive into the double iframe mechanism used by ChatGPT and MCP apps for rendering third-party UI. MCP and ChatGPT apps combine discoverability with interactive UI inside conversational agents. Views — small HTML documents with JS and CSS — are rendered as results of tool calls, advertised ahead of time via tool list calls. Inspecting ChatGPT's DOM reveals an iframe nested inside another iframe. Barthelet systematically rules out simpler alternatives: iframe srcdoc shares the parent origin, so ChatGPT's CSP with per-request script nonces blocks all third-party JS. Relaxing CSP would let apps read ChatGPT's localStorage and cookies. Sandboxing creates a null origin, removing access to origin-indexed storage. Adding allow-same-origin recreates the classic sandbox escape. Using iframe src per app domain requires updating frame-src CSP for every new app — unscalable. A proxy domain forces the host to serve untrusted code. The double iframe solution remains: an outer iframe from a controlled per-app subdomain loads a lightweight script, which injects app HTML via srcdoc into an inner iframe. Per-app subdomains prevent cross-app storage collisions while the same script content serves all subdomains, reducing infrastructure cost. The app's own CSP is provided via a meta tag in the outer iframe. Facebook used the same pattern for their app marketplace. App developers must declare all external domains their app depends on — connect-src, script-src, image-src, frame-src — in MCP app metadata, or the nested iframe CSP won't permit those calls and ChatGPT app store submissions get rejected. OpenAI's developer mode previously removed all CSP, so missing domains were only discovered at production time. Alpic built Skybridge, an open source framework on top of the official app SDK, providing end-to-end type safety, host-specific polyfills, and a CSP inspector dev tool that diffs declared domains against actual network calls live, catching missing entries before submission.
whyItMatters: The talk connects its engineering abstractions, implementation choices, and AI/product implications into one practical system view.

sections.title: Introduction and MCP Apps Overview
sections.summary: Fred introduces himself as CTO and co-founder of Alpic, an MCP hosting company. He summarizes MCP and ChatGPT apps as a new business surface area with two key properties: discoverability (app stores, in-chat surfacing) and interactive UI inside conversational agents, replacing text-only responses.

sections.title: Views: UI Rendering from Tool Calls
sections.summary: Views are small HTML documents with JS and CSS rendered as results of tool calls. Tools that support UI advertise their view resource via tool list calls, enabling caching or on-demand fetching. The host creates an iframe, injects tool results, and renders dynamic content.

sections.title: Discovering the Double Iframe
sections.summary: Curious about how ChatGPT renders third-party UI, Barthelet inspected the DOM and was surprised to find an iframe nested inside another iframe. This discovery motivated the deep dive into why each simpler approach fails.

sections.title: CSP and Iframe Fundamentals
sections.summary: Overview of Content Security Policy directives returned as response headers, focusing on frame-src (allowed iframe sources) and script-src (allowed script sources). Introduces the iframe element and its two modes: src (URL reference) and srcdoc (inline content).

sections.title: Why srcdoc and Its Variants Fail
sections.summary: srcdoc shares the parent origin and CSP, so ChatGPT's per-request script nonces block all third-party JS. Relaxing CSP lets apps read ChatGPT's localStorage and cookies. Sandboxing creates a null origin, removing all origin-indexed storage. Adding allow-same-origin restores the parent origin, creating the classic sandbox escape. All srcdoc-based approaches fail.

sections.title: Why src Per-Domain and Proxy Domain Fail
sections.summary: Using iframe src per app domain would require OpenAI to update frame-src CSP for every new app — unscalable. A single proxy domain (openaiusercontent.com) with subdomain routing could serve all apps, but forces the host to own and serve untrusted third-party code, and smaller hosts lack the infrastructure.

sections.title: The Double Iframe Solution
sections.summary: The double iframe mechanism: an outer iframe served from a controlled subdomain (unique per app) loads a lightweight script that injects the actual app HTML via srcdoc into an inner iframe. Per-app subdomains prevent cross-app storage collisions.

sections.title: Infrastructure Efficiency, App CSP, and Facebook Precedent
sections.summary: Serving the same script content for every subdomain keeps infrastructure costs low. The app's own CSP is provided via a meta tag in the outer iframe. This solution was first implemented by Facebook for their app marketplace — the same problem of rendering third-party UI inside your own application.

sections.title: Developer Requirements: Declaring Domains in Metadata
sections.summary: App developers must declare all external domains their app depends on in MCP app metadata so they are rewritten correctly into the nested iframe CSP. Key directives include connect-src (API calls), script-src, image-src, and frame-src. Barthelet compares this to early CORS struggles from 2016.

sections.title: Developer Mode and Skybridge Framework
sections.summary: OpenAI's developer mode previously removed all CSP, so missing domain declarations were only discovered at production time. Alpic built Skybridge, an open-source framework on top of the official app SDK, providing end-to-end type safety, host-specific API polyfills, and modern dev tooling including a CSP inspector.

sections.title: CSP Inspector Demo
sections.summary: Demo of a Magic 8 Ball Skybridge app with an MCP tool and view. The Skybridge dev inspector renders views live, lists tools, and compares declared metadata domains against actual network calls. Adding a fetch to an IP-location API instantly shows the domain as missing in red; adding it to metadata turns it green after reload.

sections.title: Closing and App Store Rejection Context
sections.summary: Many ChatGPT app store submissions are rejected due to missing CSP domain declarations causing apps to fail in production. Barthelet shares QR codes for slides and the Skybridge repo, and runs a ski goggles lottery for those who star the repo.

demonstrations: Skybridge CSP inspector demo: a Magic 8 Ball example app with an MCP tool and view; the inspector renders the view live, lists tools, and compares declared metadata domains against actual network calls, flagging missing domains in red and confirmed domains in green

evidence.supports: Discovery of double iframe in ChatGPT's DOM

evidence.excerpt: when you load up an iFrame with source doc attribute specified, the iFrame that you are spawning up is sharing the same origin and sharing the same therefore CSP as the host
evidence.supports: srcdoc shares parent origin and CSP, blocking third-party scripts

evidence.excerpt: you cannot use local storage. You cannot use local index DB. You cannot use cookies because those are indexed by origin
evidence.supports: Sandbox null origin removes all origin-indexed storage

evidence.excerpt: the only way to actually provide an origin to a sandboxed iFrame is to put allow same origin... and you're back to square one where you have an iFrame with exactly the right condition to escape its sandboxing

go through the double iframe mechanism. And what you will do with that is basically load the same script for everybody, which will be a simple script responsible to recover the resources and initiate an iframe with the source doc attribute
evidence.supports: Double iframe loads same script on outer frame, injects app HTML via srcdoc into inner frame

evidence.excerpt: you want to put it on various subdomains so that if your app uses any APIs that requires origin indexing like local storage or cookie, you don't have collision in between your app
evidence.supports: Per-app subdomains prevent cross-app storage collisions

evidence.excerpt: you want to be able to provide the same kind of content security policy definition to the app itself so that it can prevent execution of any such script or rendering of iframe directly inside the view
evidence.supports: App CSP is provided via meta tag in the outer iframe

evidence.excerpt: the first time this solution was implemented was back in Facebook days when they released their app marketplace, which is exactly the same problem that you have to run and render third-party UI inside the context of your own application
evidence.supports: Facebook first implemented the double iframe pattern for their app marketplace

evidence.excerpt: declare all domains your application depends upon inside the provided metadata in the MCP app spec so that you are sure that they will be rewritten correctly inside the nested iframe
